Stay on public roads or arrange permission before entering or photographing private property.", "field": "profile", "value": "San Carlos City was historically known as Binalatongan and was associated with Caboloan. The present city was created from the former municipality of San Carlos under Republic Act No. 4487 in 1965. The Province of Pangasinan describes San Carlos as a major trading center for bamboo and a leading producer of carabao mangoes. The city government presents San Carlos as an agro-industrial, commercial, educational, and tourism center. Its tourism character is centered on heritage, agriculture, mangoes, bamboo crafts, food, parks, and inland resorts."}

The city tourism site says it is held annually around the last Saturday of April and promotes the city's mangoes and bamboo products while recognizing farmers and producers. Festival activities have included float parades, street dancing, mango culinary contests, bamboo-craft competitions, variety shows, and Laro ng Lahi. Exact dates and activities can change each year, so check the City Government's announcements before traveling. San Carlos City also became known for a giant mango pie made for the 2011 festival. The city tourism site records the event as a 100-square-meter mango pie prepared using about 2,000 kilograms of ripe mangoes and shared after public viewing."}
